goal: While the orchestrate loop runs, an in-loop sweep on a bounded cadence releases lapsed claims and finalizes their stranded lifecycles so the task returns to an eligible state without any worker re-selecting that exact task, and never touches a still-live claim.

relevant: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_claims.py -- sweep_expired_claims (line ~1144, batch-release lapsed rows, no production caller today); acquire/load/list claims

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_orchestrate.py -- the `while True` loop (line ~849), the _source_reconcile_loop wiring (~833-843) to mirror cadence, _recover_claimable_stranded (~460-502) and its entry call (~825) to reuse the live-claim safety + finalize_stranded_lifecycle
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_orchestrator_claims.py -- keep green; the claims regression oracle
constraints: Wire the sweep into the steady-state loop on a bounded periodic cadence (mirror _source_reconcile_loop); the existing orchestrate-ENTRY recovery must keep working -- the in-loop sweep is additive, not a replacement
Reuse the live-claim safety of _recover_claimable_stranded: a claim with a future lease, or a task a live peer is actively running, is NEVER swept or reclaimed (criterion #2)
Finalize stranded lifecycles only through finalize_stranded_lifecycle / sanctioned store + claim APIs -- never write a status directly
Drive tests with an injected clock so lease lapse is deterministic; commit before reporting done
non_goals: Do not modify files under packages/*/tests/; do not weaken or delete assertions
Do not make the orchestrator git-aware; do not alter exactly-once execution or serialized landing (00060 invariants)
edge_cases: Eligibility after sweep must arise from the sweep itself, NOT from a coincidental re-selection of the same task id (criterion #1 grades the no-re-pick path)
A live (non-lapsed) claim and its lifecycle are byte-identical before and after a sweep cycle (criterion #2)
